# Icarus — agent guide

HTML prototypes for the **Operationalize** app, built from a design system called
**designmd**. If you are writing UI here, read this first — it is short.

**Paths below are written from the root of this folder** — the one holding `tokens.css`,
`lint.py` and `dist/`. That is true however you got it:

```
# cloned on its own (github.com/whymandesigns/icarus)
icarus/            ← you are here; prototypes live wherever you like
```
```
# inside Toptal's working layout, two sibling checkouts
icarus/
├── designmd/      ← you are here   (repo: whymandesigns/icarus)
└── features/      the prototypes   (repo: whymandesigns/opz-prototypes)
```

Only one path ever needs changing: the three `<link>` hrefs at the top of a prototype
must point at this folder, in this order —

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="PATH/TO/tokens.css" />      <!-- primitives -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="PATH/TO/semantic.css" />    <!-- aliases + reset -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="PATH/TO/components.css" />  <!-- the classes -->
```

Get them wrong and the page renders as bare HTML with no error — `lint.py` is what
catches it.

## The rules

1. **Never invent a class.** Every class must be in `designmd/dist/kit.json`. A class
   nothing defines renders as nothing, silently. If the kit has no component for what
   you need, say so rather than approximating it.
2. **Never copy markup out of `designmd/example.html`.** 88 of the classes in that file
   are the showcase's own chrome, styled in its `<style>` block and nowhere else. They
   are indistinguishable from kit classes in the markup. `.btn-cta-icon` is one, and it
   is already shipped in a prototype that way. `kit.json` lists them under
   `showcaseOnly`; the linter rejects them.
3. **Semantic tokens, never primitives.** `var(--color-bg)`, `var(--type-h1)`,
   `var(--spacing-4)` — not `var(--color-blue-500)`. Re-pointing an alias is how a theme
   changes; a primitive reference defeats that. The one sanctioned exception is
   `--color-graphite-800`, the top bar chrome, which does not change with the theme.
4. **One `.btn-primary` per page.** Every other call to action is `.btn-secondary`. Green
   is both the primary CTA and the success colour, so two of them means neither reads as
   the action.
5. **Don't write component CSS in a prototype.** If a variant is missing, add it to
   `designmd/components.css` so the next screen inherits it, then re-inline.

## Start here

Point a prototype's three stylesheet `<link>`s at this folder, build it from the
classes in `dist/kit.json`, then run from here:

```bash
python3 lint.py   <path-to-your-prototype>.html    # before you call it done
python3 inline.py <path-to-your-prototype>.html    # bake before sharing
```

`inline.py` folds the CSS, the icon sprite and the fonts into the file, so what you
share has no external dependencies and does not care where it sits.

In Toptal's working layout a prototype is `features/<kebab-name>/index.html` — always
that shape, always `index.html`. On your own, put it where you like.

## Where things are

| | |
|---|---|
| `designmd/dist/kit.json` | **the inventory** — 366 classes grouped, the attribute-driven components, and the showcase-only classes to reject. Read this to find a class. |
| `designmd/lint.py` | checks a prototype. Exit 1 on errors. |
| `designmd/DESIGN.md` | the full written system, ~15k tokens. Read sections, not the whole file. |
| `designmd/example.html` | the showcase — browse it in a browser, don't copy from it (rule 2). |
| `designmd/llms-full.txt` | this guide, the worked markup and the complete class and token inventory, ~9k tokens. **Paste this if you have no filesystem.** |
| `designmd/llms.txt` | a short index of everything above, for a tool that fetches one file. |
| `designmd/tools/build-packages.py` | regenerates `dist/` and the entry points after a stylesheet change. |
| `designmd/tools/smoke_test.py` | builds a prototype from this guide's own `<link>` block and runs lint → inline → lint. Run it after changing a tool or that snippet. |

If your tool reads its own rules file, it already has this guide: `.github/copilot-instructions.md`,
`.cursor/rules/designmd.mdc`, `.windsurfrules` and `.clinerules` are generated copies of it, so
they cannot drift. Edit `AGENTS.md` and regenerate; never edit a copy.

## Things that fail silently

- **Icons.** The three stylesheets do not carry the sprite — only `inline.py` injects it,
  so `<use href="#i-…">` renders blank until you bake. To see icons while you work, use the
  dev-time fetch in the page skeleton in `DESIGN.md` §6 "The page around them". Slugs live
  in `designmd/icons.svg`; the linter checks them.
- **Phosphor is retired.** `<i class="ph ph-x">` renders nothing. Some CSS comments still
  show it; they are stale.
- **The `example.html` script block.** Modals, drawers, dropdowns, tabs and the sheet get
  their behaviour from a delegated block there. Do not copy it whole: it is 2,286 lines
  and its tail renders the showcase's own palette swatches against elements no prototype
  has, which throws and kills every handler after it. Take the handlers you need.
- **`.topbar-title` shows nothing on a wide screen.** It is the *collapsed* title; the top
  bar is a container query that reveals it below 768px — but that is a *container*
  query on `.topbar`, which measures its content box, and the bar carries 24px of
  padding each side. So it collapses at a viewport of about **816px**, not 768.
  Same for `.topbar-menu` and
  `.topbar-cta`. Put `.topbar-menu` and `.topbar-title` in the markup from the start —
  they are invisible until the bar collapses. `.topbar-cta` is the exception: add it only
  on a page with **no** page head, because nothing hides `.page-head-actions` when the bar
  collapses, so carrying both puts two primary CTAs on screen once it does.
- **Some classes carry no CSS and are still right.** `.dropdown-trigger` is how the
  delegated script finds a dropdown's button; nothing styles it. `kit.json` lists these
  under `behaviourHooks`, beside `attributes` for the components driven by an attribute
  instead — a tooltip is `[data-tooltip]`, never `.tooltip`.

## Upstream

**Picasso is the source of truth** — Toptal's production React system
([repo](https://github.com/toptal/picasso) ·
[Storybook](https://toptal.github.io/picasso/)). designmd re-expresses its foundations as
plain CSS so a screen can exist in hours. Every token is Picasso's name and value, or is
marked `extension` with a reason in its own comment. Where the two disagree, Picasso is
right and designmd has a bug. `designmd/data/figma-map.json` carries the Storybook `storyId`
and React mapping per component.

Note the Storybook is a client-side build: `iframe.html?id=anything` returns 200, so a
request succeeding proves nothing about a story existing.

## Two consumers, one generator

designmd feeds Claude Code (this repo) and a published Design System artifact for Claude
Design. Both are generated by `tools/build-packages.py` from the three stylesheets —
`dist/kit.json`, `dist/tokens.json`, `dist/bundle.css`. They were hand-built once and
drifted badly. After changing a stylesheet, re-run it; `--check` fails when `dist/` is
stale.

---

# Markup

How the components are actually composed, and the page they need around
them. Build from these, not from example.html.

### The page around them

The snippets below are fragments. Each assumes a page that already has the three
stylesheets, the icon sprite and the handlers — and none of those is automatic.

```html
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8" />
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
  <title>Your feature</title>
  <!-- All three, in this order. Point them at wherever designmd sits. -->
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="../../designmd/tokens.css" />      <!-- primitives -->
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="../../designmd/semantic.css" />    <!-- aliases + reset -->
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="../../designmd/components.css" />  <!-- the classes -->
</head>
<body>
  … components …

  <script>
  // The sprite is NOT in the stylesheets — only inline.py injects it, so every
  // <use href="#i-…"> is blank until you bake. This covers the gap while you
  // work, and no-ops once the sprite is really in the document.
  if (!document.getElementById('i-plus')) {
    fetch('../../designmd/icons.svg').then(r => r.ok ? r.text() : null).then(svg => {
      if (!svg) return;
      const host = document.createElement('div');
      host.hidden = true; host.innerHTML = svg;
      document.body.insertBefore(host, document.body.firstChild);
    }).catch(() => {});
  }

  // Modals and drawers. Both are an overlay carrying `hidden`.
  document.addEventListener('click', e => {
    const open = e.target.closest('[data-modal-open]');
    if (open) { const el = document.getElementById(open.dataset.modalOpen);
                if (el) el.hidden = false; return; }
    const close = e.target.closest('[data-modal-close]');
    if (close) { const el = close.closest('.modal-overlay, .drawer-overlay');
                 if (el) el.hidden = true; return; }
    if (e.target.matches('.modal-overlay, .drawer-overlay')) e.target.hidden = true;
  });
  document.addEventListener('keydown', e => {
    if (e.key !== 'Escape') return;
    document.querySelectorAll('.modal-overlay:not([hidden]), .drawer-overlay:not([hidden])')
      .forEach(el => { el.hidden = true; });
  });

  // Dropdowns. The script finds the button by .dropdown-trigger, which carries no CSS.
  document.addEventListener('click', e => {
    const t = e.target.closest('.dropdown-trigger');
    document.querySelectorAll('.dropdown').forEach(d => {
      const menu = d.querySelector('.dropdown-menu');
      if (!menu) return;
      const mine = t && d.contains(t);
      menu.hidden = mine ? !menu.hidden : true;
      const btn = d.querySelector('.dropdown-trigger');
      if (btn) btn.setAttribute('aria-expanded', String(!menu.hidden));
    });
  });

  // Tabs.
  document.addEventListener('click', e => {
    const tab = e.target.closest('.tab');
    if (!tab) return;
    tab.closest('.tabs').querySelectorAll('.tab').forEach(t => {
      const on = t === tab;
      t.classList.toggle('is-active', on);
      t.setAttribute('aria-selected', String(on));
    });
  });

  // Select. NOT driven by the dropdown handler above — .input-select-trigger
  // is a different hook from .dropdown-trigger, so without this the control
  // is styled, looks finished, and does nothing when clicked.
  document.addEventListener('click', e => {
    const trigger = e.target.closest('.input-select-trigger');
    const item = e.target.closest('.input-select .dropdown-item');
    document.querySelectorAll('.input-select').forEach(sel => {
      const menu = sel.querySelector('.dropdown-menu');
      const btn = sel.querySelector('.input-select-trigger');
      if (!menu || !btn) return;
      const mine = trigger && sel.contains(trigger);
      menu.hidden = mine ? !menu.hidden : true;
      btn.setAttribute('aria-expanded', String(!menu.hidden));
    });
    if (item) {
      const sel = item.closest('.input-select');
      const value = sel.querySelector('.input-select-value');
      if (value) {
        value.textContent = (item.textContent || '').trim();
        value.classList.remove('input-select-placeholder');
      }
      sel.querySelectorAll('.dropdown-item').forEach(i =>
        i.classList.toggle('is-selected', i === item));
    }
  });

  // Side navigation — the rail toggle and the nested group expander. Both are
  // kit classes with real CSS keyed off .is-compact / aria-expanded, and
  // neither ships a handler either.
  document.addEventListener('click', e => {
    const rail = e.target.closest('.sidenav-toggle');
    if (rail) rail.closest('.sidenav').classList.toggle('is-compact');
    const group = e.target.closest('.sidenav-group-trigger');
    if (group) group.setAttribute('aria-expanded',
      String(group.getAttribute('aria-expanded') !== 'true'));
  });
  </script>
</body>
</html>
```

**A component with CSS is not a component with behaviour.** Everything above is
the complete set that ships here. The sheet, the date picker, dropzones, tag
inputs, toasts, segmented controls and tree-table row toggles are all styled by
the kit and all inert until you write their handler — their markup looks
finished and does nothing. Those handlers live in `example.html`'s `<script>`
block: take the ones you need, and do **not** copy the whole block, because its
tail renders the showcase's own palette swatches against elements no prototype
has, throws, and stops every later handler attaching.

### Common snippets

```html
<!-- Button -->
<button class="btn btn-primary">Continue</button>
<button class="btn btn-secondary">Cancel</button>
<button class="btn btn-ghost">Skip</button>
<button class="btn btn-danger">Delete</button>

<!-- Field + Input -->
<label class="field">
  <span class="field-label">Email</span>
  <input class="input" type="email" placeholder="you@example.com" />
  <span class="field-hint">We'll never share your email.</span>
</label>

<!-- Card -->
<article class="card">
  <h3 class="card-title">Title</h3>
  <p class="card-body">Body text.</p>
</article>

<!-- Badge -->
<span class="badge badge-success">Active</span>

<!-- Alert -->
<div class="alert alert-warning" role="alert">
  <svg class="icon alert-icon"><use href="#i-warning"></use></svg>
  <p class="alert-message">Your trial expires in 5 days.</p>
  <div class="alert-actions">
    <button class="btn btn-xs btn-primary">Upgrade</button>
  </div>
  <button class="alert-close" type="button" aria-label="Close"><svg class="icon"><use href="#i-x"></use></svg></button>
</div>

<!-- Tabs -->
<div class="tabs" role="tablist">
  <button class="tab is-active" role="tab" aria-selected="true" aria-controls="p-1" id="t-1" type="button">Overview</button>
  <button class="tab" role="tab" aria-selected="false" aria-controls="p-2" id="t-2" type="button">Activity</button>
</div>
<div role="tabpanel" id="p-1" aria-labelledby="t-1">…</div>
<div role="tabpanel" id="p-2" aria-labelledby="t-2" hidden>…</div>

<!-- Tooltip -->
<button class="btn btn-secondary" data-tooltip="Save your changes" data-placement="top">Save</button>

<!-- Type helpers -->
<h1 class="h1">Page title</h1>
<p class="body">Body copy.</p>
<span class="caption">Caption</span>
```

The ones below are the structures that cannot be guessed from a class name — which
wraps which, and what actually opens a thing.

```html
<!-- Top bar.
     .topbar-menu, .topbar-title and .topbar-cta are the COLLAPSED layout, revealed
     below 768px of the bar's OWN width, so they show nothing on a wide screen. Put
     the menu and title in from the start. Use .topbar-cta only on a page with no
     page head, or both primaries appear at once when the bar collapses. -->
<header class="topbar">
  <button class="btn btn-icon-only btn-ghost topbar-menu" type="button" aria-label="Menu">
    <svg class="btn-icon"><use href="#i-list"></use></svg>
  </button>
  <div class="topbar-brand">
    <img class="topbar-brand-logo" src="../../designmd/assets/logo.svg" alt="Operationalize" />
  </div>
  <span class="topbar-title">Page name</span>
  <div class="topbar-search">
    <svg class="icon search-icon"><use href="#i-magnifying-glass"></use></svg>
    <input class="topbar-search-input" type="search" placeholder="Search" aria-label="Search" />
  </div>
  <div class="topbar-actions">
    <span class="avatar avatar-sm">MV</span>
  </div>
</header>

<!-- Page head — and the page's one .btn-primary. -->
<div class="page-head">
  <div class="page-head-main">
    <div class="page-head-title">
      <h1 class="page-head-heading">Invoices</h1>
      <span class="count-badge count-badge-lg count-badge-secondary">4</span>
    </div>
    <p class="page-head-subtitle">One sentence of context.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="page-head-actions">
    <button class="btn btn-primary" type="button">
      <svg class="btn-icon"><use href="#i-plus"></use></svg>New invoice
    </button>
  </div>
</div>

<!-- Input with a leading icon. The WRAPPER carries .input-icon and the side;
     the glyph is a sibling of the input, not a child. -->
<div class="input-icon input-icon-left">
  <svg class="icon input-icon-glyph"><use href="#i-magnifying-glass"></use></svg>
  <input class="input" type="search" placeholder="Filter invoices" aria-label="Filter" />
</div>

<!-- Toolbar — a filter row above a table. .toolbar-search on the input wrapper
     makes it take the free space. -->
<div class="toolbar">
  <div class="input-icon input-icon-left toolbar-search">
    <svg class="icon input-icon-glyph"><use href="#i-magnifying-glass"></use></svg>
    <input class="input" type="text" placeholder="Search by name or owner" aria-label="Search" />
  </div>
  <button class="btn btn-secondary" type="button">
    <svg class="icon"><use href="#i-funnel"></use></svg>Filters
  </button>
</div>

<!-- Table. .table goes on the <table>; .table-scroll is the wrapper. -->
<div class="table-scroll">
  <table class="table">
    <thead>
      <tr><th>Invoice</th><th>Status</th><th style="text-align: right">Actions</th></tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
      <tr>
        <td><span class="cell-title">INV-1041</span></td>
        <td><span class="badge badge-success">Paid</span></td>
        <td>
          <div class="cell-actions">
            <button class="btn btn-icon-only btn-ghost btn-xs" type="button"
                    aria-label="Open INV-1041" data-modal-open="invoice-detail">
              <svg class="btn-icon"><use href="#i-arrow-right"></use></svg>
            </button>
          </div>
        </td>
      </tr>
    </tbody>
  </table>
</div>

<!-- A person in a table cell. -->
<div class="cell-user">
  <span class="avatar avatar-md">AS</span>
  <div class="cell-user-meta">
    <span class="cell-user-name">Anna Schmidt</span>
    <span class="cell-user-role">anna@example.com</span>
  </div>
</div>

<!-- Drawer. The OVERLAY WRAPS the panel and carries `hidden`. Opening is
     data-modal-open="<overlay id>" on any trigger; closing is data-modal-close.
     There is no .is-open for this.
     Use the DRAWER's own header/body/footer — unlike the modal's they carry the
     dividers and even padding a full-height panel needs. (example.html builds its
     drawers from .modal-header and .modal-body; that is the showcase being
     inconsistent, not the pattern to copy.)
     Widths: .drawer-narrow .drawer-regular .drawer-medium .drawer-wide
     .drawer-ultra. A modal is the same shape with
     .modal-overlay > .modal.modal-sm and the .modal-* parts. -->
<div class="drawer-overlay" id="invoice-detail" hidden>
  <aside class="drawer drawer-regular" role="dialog" aria-modal="true"
         aria-labelledby="invoice-detail-title">
    <header class="drawer-header">
      <h2 class="modal-title" id="invoice-detail-title">INV-1041</h2>
      <button class="btn btn-icon-only btn-ghost btn-xs modal-close" type="button"
              data-modal-close aria-label="Close">
        <svg class="btn-icon"><use href="#i-x"></use></svg>
      </button>
    </header>
    <div class="drawer-body"><p class="body">Detail goes here.</p></div>
    <footer class="drawer-footer">
      <button class="btn btn-secondary" type="button" data-modal-close>Close</button>
    </footer>
  </aside>
</div>

<!-- Dropdown. .dropdown-trigger carries no CSS — the delegated script finds the
     button by it. -->
<div class="dropdown">
  <button class="btn btn-secondary dropdown-trigger" type="button" aria-expanded="false">
    Actions <svg class="btn-icon"><use href="#i-caret-down"></use></svg>
  </button>
  <div class="dropdown-menu dropdown-menu-end" hidden>
    <button class="dropdown-item" type="button">Download PDF</button>
    <div class="dropdown-divider"></div>
    <button class="dropdown-item dropdown-item-danger" type="button">Void invoice</button>
  </div>
</div>

<!-- App shell — sidenav beside the page. Goes BELOW the top bar and replaces
     <main class="page">. Add .is-compact to .sidenav for the collapsed rail.
     NOTE: .app-shell ships with the showcase's 560px frame, so a real page
     needs the override in the components.css docblock above .app-shell —
     without it you get a bordered 560px box floating in the viewport. -->
<div class="app-shell">
  <aside class="sidenav">
    <button class="sidenav-toggle" type="button" aria-label="Toggle navigation">
      <svg><use href="#i-chevron-left"></use></svg>
    </button>
    <ul class="sidenav-list">
      <li><a class="sidenav-item is-active" href="#">
        <svg class="sidenav-item-icon"><use href="#i-cpu-2"></use></svg>
        <span class="sidenav-item-label">Processes</span>
      </a></li>
    </ul>
  </aside>
  <main class="app-shell-main">…</main>
</div>
```

For the full inventory with every modifier and live demos, open `example.html` — it's the complete picture of what designmd offers and how each component composes. For what a component *is*, though, the authority is Picasso: its [Storybook](https://toptal.github.io/picasso/) for behaviour and props, and `packages/base/<Component>/src/` for the implementation. `data/figma-map.json` carries the `storyId` for each one.

# Complete inventory

Generated from the stylesheets. Everything the kit defines is below; if a
name is not here, it does not exist.

## Classes (366)

## Attribute-driven components

Not every component is a class.

- `[data-align]` — values: center, end
- `[data-collapsible]`
- `[data-level]` — values: 0, 1, 2
- `[data-placement]` — values: bottom, left, right
- `[data-theme]` — values: dark
- `[data-tooltip]`
- `[data-tooltip-style]` — values: regular
- `[data-variant]` — values: muted
- `[data-component]`
- `[data-datepicker]`
- `[data-dropzone]`
- `[data-fail]`
- `[data-modal-close]`
- `[data-modal-open]`
- `[data-sheet]`
- `[data-slider-output]`
- `[data-type]`

## Behaviour hooks

No CSS of their own, but the delegated script finds its targets by them.

.datepicker-prev · .dropdown-trigger · .editor-counter-text · .page-view

## Never use these

88 classes that example.html styles in its own
`<style>` block and nowhere else. They look like kit classes in markup.
